classification.difficultyReason: Distinguishes parabolic traces using implicit parameter restrictions and the marked point at t = 1.

content.prompt: Match the following parametric equations and curves. The point where $t=1$ is marked.

spec.description: Full upward parabola, arrowheads at both upper ends, black axes and a filled point close to the vertex on the right branch. Roman label below.
spec.mathematics: y=x^2 for all real x; marked point (1,1). The same coordinate units and bounding box are used for diagrams I, II and III.
spec.answerVisibility: Curve, axes, unlabelled marked point and diagram label are permanent student-visible givens. No equation, numeric ticks or origin label is printed.

spec.description: Full upward parabola with both upper arrowheads and a filled point on the left branch at the same height as diagram I's point.
spec.mathematics: y=x^2 for all real x; marked point (-1,1). Common scale with I and III.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent student-visible graph, unlabelled marked point and Roman label. No equation, numeric ticks or origin label is printed.

spec.description: Full upward parabola with both upper arrowheads and a filled point higher on the right branch than diagram I's point.
spec.mathematics: y=x^2 for all real x; marked point (2,4). Common scale with I and II.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent student-visible graph, unlabelled marked point and Roman label. No equation, numeric ticks or origin label is printed.

spec.description: Short bounded parabola segment on both sides of the origin, without curve-end arrows or endpoint markers, with a filled point on its right branch.
spec.mathematics: y=x^2 for -1<=x<=1; marked point (cos 1,cos^2 1), with 1 measured in radians.
spec.answerVisibility: Bounded trace, unlabelled marked point, axes and Roman label are permanent student-visible givens. Bounds and point coordinates are not printed.

spec.description: Right-hand parabola branch beginning at the origin, one upper curve arrow and a filled point on the branch. No separate origin marker.
spec.answerVisibility: Branch, axes, unlabelled marked point and Roman label are permanent student-visible givens. No restriction or point coordinates are printed.

spec.description: Upward parabola with both upper arrowheads, a white-centred open origin marker and a filled point on the right branch.
spec.mathematics: y=x^2 for x!=0; marked point (1,1). The open marker excludes (0,0).
spec.answerVisibility: Curve, excluded-origin marker, axes, unlabelled marked point and Roman label are permanent student-visible givens. No equation or numeric ticks are printed.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=4t^2\\y&=(2t)^2\\y&=x^2\end{align*}$$
All real $x$ are possible. At $t=1$, $(x,y)=(2,4)$, so the matching curve is (III).

$$\begin{align*}y&=\frac1{t^2}\\y&=\left(\frac1t\right)^2\\y&=x^2\end{align*}$$
Since $t\ne0$, $x=\frac{1}{t}$ takes every nonzero real value. The origin is excluded. At $t=1$, $(x,y)=(1,1)$, so the matching curve is (VI).
$t=x$, so $y=x^2$ for all real $x$. At $t=1$, $(x,y)=(1,1)$, so the matching curve is (I).

$$\begin{align*}t&=x^2\\y&=x^2\end{align*}$$
Since $x=\sqrt t\ge0$, only the right-hand branch is traced, including the origin. At $t=1$, $(x,y)=(1,1)$, so the matching curve is (V).

$t=-x$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=(-x)^2\\y&=x^2\end{align*}$$
All real $x$ are possible. At $t=1$, $(x,y)=(-1,1)$, so the matching curve is (II).

$$\begin{align*}y&=(\cos t)^2\\y&=x^2\end{align*}$$
Since $-1\le\cos t\le1$, only the bounded segment $-1\le x\le1$ is traced. At $t=1$, the point is $(\cos1,\cos^21)$ on the right branch, so the matching curve is (IV).
